hunks.baseline: The march went smoothly. The heavy snow that had fallen during our last reconnaissance mission had melted away long ago, and command moved us while conserving as much of the troops’ strength as possible.
hunks.sol: The march went smoothly. The heavy snow that had fallen during our last reconnaissance mission had melted long ago, and command set a pace that conserved as much of the troops’ strength as possible.

hunks.baseline: “At this rate, we’ll arrive in Jeongyang by tomorrow at the latest.”
hunks.sol: “At this rate, we’ll reach Jeongyang by tomorrow at the latest.”

hunks.baseline: I blinked at the oddly familiar man’s words.
hunks.sol: I blinked at the oddly familiar man.

hunks.baseline: Judging by his clothes, he wasn’t from the Jin Family of Taiyuan. Aside from the reconnaissance squad, most of the people in the rear guard were martial artists from the newly allied small and mid-sized sects, so that made sense.
hunks.sol: Judging by his clothes, he wasn’t from the Jin Family of Taiyuan. Aside from the reconnaissance squad, most of the rear guard consisted of martial artists from the newly allied small and mid-sized sects, so that made sense.

hunks.baseline: Gwak Jun of the Three Paths Sect? It was on the tip of my tongue.
hunks.sol: Gwak Jun of the Samdo Sect? It felt like I should remember him.

hunks.baseline: Gwak Jun gave me a friendly smile and went on.
hunks.sol: Gwak Jun gave me a friendly smile and continued.

hunks.baseline: “Because there’d be fewer chances to distinguish ourselves. Isn’t this the chance for an unknown grunt like me to make a name for himself?”
hunks.sol: “Because there’d be fewer chances to distinguish ourselves. Isn’t this the perfect opportunity for an unknown grunt like me to make a name for himself?”

hunks.baseline: There were two possibilities in cases like this. Either he’d been through so many battles that he’d grown nerves of steel, or he was simply fearless.
hunks.sol: There were two possibilities in cases like this. Either he’d fought in so many battles that he’d developed nerves of steel, or he simply had no fear.

hunks.baseline: I raised my **Qi Sense**.
hunks.sol: I activated **Qi Sense**.

hunks.baseline: *Oh. He’s got some skill.*
hunks.sol: *Oh. He’s pretty good.*

hunks.baseline: At Level 40, he was at least First Rate. He couldn’t exactly go around bragging he was a master, but it was more than enough to feel wronged about being stuck in the rear.
hunks.sol: At Level 40, he was at least First Rate. He couldn’t exactly go around bragging that he was a master, but he was good enough to resent being stuck in the rear.

hunks.baseline: “Half of the enemy troops were recruited in a hurry. They’ve dragged in every kind of deadweight, and they must have force-marched to join the main force. They won’t stand a chance against the elites of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Three Paths Sect.”
hunks.sol: “Half of the enemy troops were recruited in a hurry. They’ve dragged in every kind of deadweight, and they must have force-marched to join the main force. They won’t stand a chance against the elites of the Jin Family of Taiyuan and the Samdo Sect.”

hunks.baseline: His words sounded plausible enough.
hunks.sol: His argument sounded plausible enough.

hunks.baseline: *If you leave out the part about the Three Paths Sect being elite.*
hunks.sol: *If you leave out the part about the Samdo Sect being elite.*

hunks.baseline: I nodded half-heartedly.
hunks.sol: I nodded halfheartedly.

hunks.baseline: “And we have Peak masters superior to the enemy’s as well. There’s the Lesser Family Head and Great Hero Wipeng, of course, but the reputation of the Blade of Flowers has spread throughout the Central Plains, hasn’t it?”
hunks.sol: “And our Peak masters are superior to theirs. There’s the Lesser Family Head and Great Hero Wipeng, of course, but the fame of the Blade of Flowers has spread throughout the Central Plains, hasn’t it?”

hunks.baseline: The Jin Family of Taiyuan had three Peak masters. Exclude Jin Wikyung and Wipeng, and only one person was left.
hunks.sol: The Jin Family of Taiyuan had three Peak masters. Excluding Jin Wikyung and Wipeng, only one person remained.

hunks.baseline: Gwak Jun’s next words were nothing but praise. Title after title, name after name of masters the Head Elder had cut down in his youth, decades ago, came spilling out.
hunks.sol: Everything Gwak Jun said next was praise. Title after title, name after name of masters the Head Elder had cut down in his youth decades ago came spilling out.

hunks.baseline: A war hero from the past. Listening to Gwak Jun, he sounded like a chivalrous hero among chivalrous heroes—a man who loved justice and couldn’t stand to see injustice go unpunished…
hunks.sol: A war hero from the past. Listening to Gwak Jun, he sounded like the noblest of chivalrous heroes—a man who loved justice and couldn’t stand to see injustice go unpunished…

hunks.baseline: *Then why do I feel so uneasy every time I see him?*
hunks.sol: *Then why do I feel uneasy every time I see him?*

hunks.baseline: Maybe it was the first impression, but I disliked the Head Elder.
hunks.sol: Maybe it was because of my first impression, but I didn’t like the Head Elder.

hunks.baseline: That peculiar air of his. The strange gaze that bored straight through people. The fact that he had formed a political faction against Jin Wikyung.
hunks.sol: That peculiar air of his. The strange gaze that seemed to bore straight through people. The fact that he had formed a political faction in opposition to Jin Wikyung.

hunks.baseline: And yet after that, the Head Elder had thrown his full support behind Jin Wikyung, and the Jin Family of Taiyuan had been able to pull tight together, inside and out.
hunks.sol: Since then, however, the Head Elder had thrown his full support behind Jin Wikyung, allowing the Jin Family of Taiyuan to present a united front both inside and out.

hunks.baseline: The Head Elder was currently leading the vanguard alongside Jin Wikyung. If he really was as skilled as the rumors claimed, tomorrow’s battle would be that much easier.
hunks.sol: The Head Elder was currently leading the vanguard alongside Jin Wikyung. If he truly was as skilled as the rumors claimed, tomorrow’s battle would be that much easier.

hunks.baseline: “Just thinking of Great Hero Blade of Flowers sweeping the battlefield tomorrow already has my heart racing.”
hunks.sol: “Just thinking about the Blade of Flowers sweeping across the battlefield tomorrow is already making my heart race.”

hunks.baseline: Gwak Jun shuddered like a man taking a piss after three days.
hunks.sol: Gwak Jun shuddered like a man finally taking a piss after holding it for three days.

hunks.baseline: And where was he getting the confidence that we were going to win?
hunks.sol: And where was he getting all this confidence that we were going to win?

hunks.baseline: “You’re certain of victory.”
hunks.sol: “You sound certain we’ll win.”

hunks.baseline: “If we lose, we’re in big trouble.”
hunks.sol: “If we lose, we’ll be in big trouble.”

hunks.baseline: Judging by everything the Mount Heng Sword Sect had done so far, they would turn not only the Jin Family of Taiyuan but the small and mid-sized sects allied with us into a wasteland.
hunks.sol: Judging by everything the Mount Heng Sword Sect had done so far, they would raze not only the Jin Family of Taiyuan but every small and mid-sized sect allied with us.

hunks.baseline: As I stared at him, speechless, Gwak Jun flashed me a grin.
hunks.sol: As I stared at him in disbelief, Gwak Jun flashed me a grin.

hunks.baseline: One sentence, packed with conviction.
hunks.sol: The words rang with absolute conviction.

hunks.baseline: When Gwak Jun left it at that and moved away, Hyuk Mujin came up and asked,
hunks.sol: After Gwak Jun walked away, Hyuk Mujin came over and asked,

hunks.baseline: “There’s this guy. Overflowing with confidence.”
hunks.sol: “Just some guy overflowing with confidence.”

hunks.baseline: I didn’t like him, in more ways than one.
hunks.sol: I didn’t like him for several reasons.

hunks.baseline: *Well, it wasn’t as though I’d have to talk to him again.*
hunks.sol: *Well, it wasn’t as though I’d ever have to talk to him again.*

hunks.baseline: Time passed quickly. On the second night after we began the march, we reached Honju, and Jin Wikyung gathered the command staff for a meeting. He was holding a small slip of paper.
hunks.sol: Time passed quickly. On the second night of the march, we reached Honju, and Jin Wikyung gathered the command staff for a meeting. He held a small slip of paper in one hand.

hunks.baseline: I couldn’t understand it. If we had attacked the main force before the reinforcements joined them, the fight would have been much easier.
hunks.sol: I didn’t understand. If we had attacked the main force before the reinforcements joined them, the battle would have been much easier.

hunks.baseline: Sure enough, Jin Wikyung went on.
hunks.sol: Sure enough, Jin Wikyung continued.

hunks.baseline: “The enemy reinforcements that just joined them are exhausted, and their food is running out. If we take Jeongyang’s high ground first tomorrow, the Mount Heng Sword Sect Leader will have a choice to make. Fall back, or clash.”
hunks.sol: “The enemy reinforcements are exhausted, and their food supplies are nearly gone. If we seize the advantageous ground at Jeongyang first tomorrow, the Sect Leader of the Mount Heng Sword Sect will face a choice. Retreat or clash with us.”

hunks.baseline: The next moment, Jin Wikyung’s gaze shifted to me.
hunks.sol: The next moment, Jin Wikyung looked at me.

hunks.baseline: I was caught off guard, but the answer was already there. If he were the kind of man to fall back at this point, he would have done so long ago.
hunks.sol: The sudden question caught me off guard, but the answer was obvious. If he were the kind of man to retreat at this point, he would have done so long ago.

hunks.baseline: “I think he’ll clash.”
hunks.sol: “I think he’ll clash with us.”

hunks.baseline: Twice our numbers, and they weren’t behind us in Peak masters either. From the enemy’s side, they would want to end this fight as fast as possible.
hunks.sol: They had nearly twice our numbers, and they weren’t behind us in Peak masters either. From the enemy’s perspective, the best option was to end the battle quickly and decisively.

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung smiled, pleased, and traced a finger across the topographic map on the table.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung smiled in satisfaction and traced a finger across the topographic map spread over the table.

hunks.baseline: “Eight Spring Gorge. Jar-shaped, with a narrow, steep mouth. The mounted bandits will have to abandon their prized horses.”
hunks.sol: “Eight Spring Gorge. Jar-shaped, with a narrow, steep entrance. The mounted bandits will have to abandon their prized horses.”

hunks.baseline: “They’ll have to abandon their lives too.”
hunks.sol: “They’ll have to abandon their lives as well.”

hunks.baseline: “The enemy will fight with their lives on the line as well. This much won’t be enough.”
hunks.sol: “The enemy will fight with their lives on the line. This alone will not be enough.”

hunks.baseline: “I’ve hidden some hundred horn bows on the cliffs above the gorge.”
hunks.sol: “I’ve hidden a hundred horn bows atop the cliffs overlooking the gorge.”

hunks.baseline: *When the hell did he hide those?*
hunks.sol: *When the hell did he hide those there?*

hunks.baseline: “Right after our victory at Honju. Thanks to a resourceful ally.”
hunks.sol: “Right after our victory at Honju. Thanks to a resourceful helper.”

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung looked straight at me as he said it.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung looked straight at me as he spoke.

hunks.baseline: She had been helping us constantly from places we couldn’t see. Of course, Jin Wikyung was impressive too, for drawing a picture this big.
hunks.sol: She had been helping us constantly from behind the scenes. Of course, Jin Wikyung was impressive too for planning this far ahead.

hunks.baseline: A build like a human meat grinder, and a sharp mind to go with it. Suddenly I wanted to call him big brother.
hunks.sol: A body like a human meat grinder and a brilliant mind to go with it. Suddenly I wanted to call him hyung.

hunks.baseline: “The Lesser Family Head…!”
hunks.sol: “Lesser Family Head…!”

hunks.baseline: The tent went hot under the burning gazes of those dark, burly men.
hunks.sol: The tent grew hot beneath the burning gazes of all those rough-looking men.

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung swept a heavy look over everyone assembled.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung swept his solemn gaze over everyone assembled.

hunks.baseline: No one objected. The Head Elder was the first to rise, then gave Jin Wikyung a fist-in-palm salute.
hunks.sol: No one objected. The Head Elder was the first to rise and give Jin Wikyung a fist-in-palm salute.

hunks.baseline: That was the end of the meeting. As I left the tent, a familiar voice bored into my ear.
hunks.sol: That brought the meeting to an end. As I left the tent, a familiar voice pierced my ear.

hunks.baseline: —Don’t forget what I told you yesterday.
hunks.sol: —Do not forget what I told you yesterday.

hunks.baseline: I stiffened for a moment. Then I gave a small nod.
hunks.sol: I stiffened for a moment, then gave a small nod.

hunks.baseline: And at dawn that day, three hundred martial artists from the Jin Family of Taiyuan and one hundred fifty reinforcements from the small and mid-sized sects—four hundred fifty in all—set out for the gorge.
hunks.sol: At dawn, three hundred martial artists from the Jin Family of Taiyuan and one hundred fifty reinforcements from the small and mid-sized sects—four hundred fifty in all—departed for the gorge.

hunks.baseline: *Still, this was the end, and I hadn’t even said a proper goodbye.*
hunks.sol: *Even though this was goodbye, I never got to say it properly.*

hunks.baseline: I climbed a hill and stared endlessly at the winding line of torches.
hunks.sol: I climbed a hill and stared for a long time at the winding line of torches.

hunks.baseline: “You startled me. What’s going on?”
hunks.sol: “You startled me. What happened?”

hunks.baseline: “What do you mean, what? You look like a living corpse. Did you not sleep?”
hunks.sol: “What do you mean, what? You look like a walking corpse. Didn’t you sleep?”

hunks.baseline: That was a lie. I hadn’t slept a wink. I had planted myself on a rock and stared at the System Window all night.
hunks.sol: That was a lie. I hadn’t slept a wink. I had spent the entire night perched on a rock, staring at the System Window.

hunks.baseline: Counting down to the moment that had finally come right up to my nose.
hunks.sol: Eagerly awaiting the moment that had finally drawn near.

hunks.baseline: I never thought the number 1 could feel this precious.
hunks.sol: I never knew the number one could feel so precious.

hunks.baseline: In a voice that had aged all of a sudden, I muttered,
hunks.sol: In a voice that seemed to have aged overnight, I muttered,

hunks.baseline: “I’m going, I’m going, going home now…”
hunks.sol: “I’m going, I’m going, now I’m going home…”

hunks.baseline: Hyuk Mujin clicked his tongue, then his eyes went round.
hunks.sol: Hyuk Mujin clicked his tongue, then his eyes widened.

hunks.baseline: “What’s that? I’ve never seen those before.”
hunks.sol: “What are those? I’ve never seen them before.”

hunks.baseline: “This?”
hunks.sol: “These?”

hunks.baseline: I pointed in turn at the old book and the small case sitting on the rock.
hunks.sol: I pointed in turn at the old book and the small box resting on the rock.

hunks.baseline: “Hah. Really?”
hunks.sol: “Gasp. Really?”

hunks.baseline: I explained it weakly to the guy whose eyes were halfway out of his head.
hunks.sol: I listlessly explained to the guy whose eyes were halfway out of their sockets.

hunks.baseline: “The manual’s a Supreme Peak martial art, and if you absorb the elixir right, it’s half a jiazi.”
hunks.sol: “The manual contains a Supreme Peak martial art, and if you absorb the elixir properly, it’ll give you half a jiazi.”

hunks.baseline: “But they say if you take the elixir wrong, you’ll burn to death. You want it?”
hunks.sol: “But if you take the elixir wrong, apparently you’ll burn to death. Want it?”

hunks.baseline: Judging by that unimpressed face and the snout sticking out a good few feet, he didn’t believe a damn word I was saying.
hunks.sol: Judging by his unimpressed face and the way his lips were sticking out a mile, he didn’t believe a damn word I was saying.

hunks.baseline: *Well, if someone suddenly came at me with a Supreme Peak martial art and a thirty-year Fireball elixir, I’d figure it was a joke too.*
hunks.sol: *Well, if someone suddenly came at me with a Supreme Peak martial art and a thirty-year Fireball elixir, I’d assume it was a joke too.*

hunks.baseline: “You really won’t eat it? It’s good stuff.”
hunks.sol: “You really don’t want it? It’s good stuff.”

hunks.baseline: “Oh, I’m fine. Learn plenty of that Supreme Peak martial art, and be sure to chew your elixir thoroughly.”
hunks.sol: “Oh, I’m fine. Learn plenty of that Supreme Peak martial art, and make sure you chew your elixir thoroughly.”

hunks.baseline: “Of course. You’re the Hidden Dragon.”
hunks.sol: “Of course not. You’re the Hidden Dragon.”

hunks.baseline: Normally I would have smacked him in the back of the head. Right now I didn’t feel much of anything.
hunks.sol: Normally, I would have smacked him in the back of the head. Right now, I didn’t feel much of anything.

hunks.baseline: At the same time, I felt strange. Was it the aftereffect of everything I’d been through? It had only been a little over a month, but it felt distant, as if I’d been here a year.
hunks.sol: At the same time, I felt strangely wistful. Maybe it was an aftereffect of everything I’d been through. I had only been here for a little over a month, yet it felt as though a whole year had passed.

hunks.baseline: I started tracing back through old memories.
hunks.sol: I began tracing back through my memories.

hunks.baseline: That was where I met Wolhwa for the first time and realized I was trapped in this game. Even now, thinking about that moment gave me goose bumps.
hunks.sol: That was where I met Wolhwa and realized I was trapped in this game. Even now, thinking back on that moment gave me goose bumps.

hunks.baseline: “Hmm. Just thought of the old days.”
hunks.sol: “Hmm. Just thinking about the old days.”

hunks.baseline: “Nope. Not telling. Get back already.”
hunks.sol: “Nope. Not telling. Now hurry back.”

hunks.baseline: “What am I, some back-alley punk? Just because your martial arts are a bit strong, you think you can oppress people like this?”
hunks.sol: “What are you, some back-alley thug? Just because your martial arts are a bit stronger, you think you can bully people like this?”

hunks.baseline: As Hyuk Mujin threw a fit, everyone’s eyes turned toward us. Even the reconnaissance-squad members who had been watching like it was none of their business jumped in.
hunks.sol: As Hyuk Mujin threw a fit, everyone turned to look at us. Even the reconnaissance-squad members who had been watching from the sidelines joined in.

hunks.baseline: “Dunno. The deputy squad leader must have done something wrong.”
hunks.sol: “Dunno. The deputy captain must have done something wrong.”

hunks.baseline: “But should we even be doing this?”
hunks.sol: “But should we really be acting like this?”

hunks.baseline: At someone’s words, silence fell for a moment.
hunks.sol: At someone’s words, silence fell.

hunks.baseline: The tension and fear they had been holding down with forced smiles hung in the air. Even I, who would soon be going back to the real world, felt uneasy with Jin Wikyung’s face flickering through my mind. How much worse must it be for these guys?
hunks.sol: The tension and fear they had been suppressing with forced smiles rose to the surface. Even I, who would soon be returning to the real world, felt uneasy whenever Jin Wikyung’s face came to mind. How much worse must it be for these guys?

hunks.baseline: “I trust my big brother.”
hunks.sol: “I trust my hyung.”
*Hyung.*

hunks.baseline: *Big brother.* This time, I put my heart into the word.
hunks.sol: This time, I put my heart into the word.

hunks.baseline: Jin Wikyung had been the greatest source of strength I’d had in this place. Maybe I simply wanted to shake off that unease, even if only like this.
hunks.sol: Jin Wikyung had been my greatest source of strength in this place. Maybe I simply wanted to shake off that unease, even if only by saying it aloud.

hunks.baseline: The faces that had stiffened for a moment eased.
hunks.sol: The tension eased from everyone’s faces.

hunks.baseline: “I trust the squad leader more.”
hunks.sol: “I trust the Captain more.”

hunks.baseline: “Wow. Deputy squad leader, that side-switching of yours is really something.”
hunks.sol: “Wow. Deputy Captain, you’re awfully quick to switch sides.”

hunks.baseline: “You little bastards. Is there anyone here who doesn’t owe the squad leader their life?”
hunks.sol: “You little bastards. Is there anyone here who doesn’t owe the Captain their life?”

hunks.baseline: “I trust the squad leader too. Honestly, I knew all along, even when you were playing the thug. I thought, *Ah, that man is the Sleeping Dragon.* I could tell right away.”
hunks.sol: “I trust the Captain too. Honestly, I knew all along, even when you were pretending to be a thug. I thought, *Ah, that man is the Hidden Dragon.* I could tell right away.”

hunks.baseline: I felt strange.
hunks.sol: It felt strange.

hunks.baseline: *They say even dried squid gives water if you squeeze it. Who knew I’d feel something like this toward NPCs in a game?*
hunks.sol: *Even dried squid gives up water if you squeeze it hard enough. Who knew I’d feel something like this toward NPCs in a game?*

hunks.baseline: Suddenly I wondered about Jin Wikyung, somewhere beyond those mountains. Had the battle started? If it had, which side was winning?
hunks.sol: Suddenly, I found myself wondering about Jin Wikyung, somewhere beyond those mountains. Had the battle started? If so, which side was winning?

hunks.baseline: And I wasn’t the only one thinking that.
hunks.sol: And I wasn’t the only one thinking about it.

hunks.baseline: It was Gwak Jun of the Three Paths Sect. Unlike before, he was wearing black martial robes.
hunks.sol: It was Gwak Jun of the Samdo Sect. Unlike before, he was dressed in black martial robes.

hunks.baseline: *Was that what this guy originally wore?*
hunks.sol: *Was that what he was wearing before?*

hunks.baseline: At my look, Gwak Jun shrugged.
hunks.sol: When he noticed me looking, Gwak Jun shrugged.

hunks.baseline: “I like this sort of thing. Easy to move in, and even if a little blood splatters, it doesn’t show. You all feel the same, right?”
hunks.sol: “I like this sort of thing. It’s easy to move in, and even if a little blood splatters on it, no one can tell. You agree, don’t you?”

hunks.baseline: That last question wasn’t aimed at us. It was for the martial artists of the Three Paths Sect whom he led. Every last one of them had changed into black, and they nodded without a word.
hunks.sol: The last question wasn’t directed at us. It was meant for the Samdo Sect martial artists under his command. Every last one of them had changed into black, and they nodded without a word.

hunks.baseline: “Apparently so.”
hunks.sol: “Apparently they do.”

hunks.baseline: Gwak Jun smiled, satisfied, then turned to me.
hunks.sol: Gwak Jun smiled in satisfaction, then turned to me.

hunks.baseline: *What the fuck is this bastard talking about right now?*
hunks.sol: *What the fuck is this bastard talking about?*
